clue.text: A quarter, or half, audibly expressed relief

indicators.note: audibly says the word for expressed relief is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to express relief with a long breath out is to sigh, past tense sighed

explanation.surface: Someone lets out a breath of relief that sounds like a quarter or a half of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' signals that SIGHED is heard, and it sounds just like the four letters wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A side can be one of the two halves of a field or one of four quarters of a square, a facing part.

clue.text: Sign of arachnid without sting?

indicators.note: a scorpion's sting is in its tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a scorpion is an arachnid

explanation.surface: Which star sign is a scorpion that has had its sting removed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without sting' means removing the tail, and the tail of the word is its last letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighth sign of the zodiac, represented by a scorpion.

clue.text: During an illness, almost over, trouble a spiritual leader

indicators.note: during says the word for trouble sits in the middle of the reversed illness
over says the words an and almost-illness are turned backwards

parts.note: an gives the single letter

indicators.note: almost says the word for illness loses its last letter

parts.note: a malady is an illness
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A holy leader is troubled while recovering from a sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a spiritual leader' is the definition; 'over' turns back the whole of 'an illness, almost', and 'During' places the trouble within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan Buddhist head is a spiritual leader, the best known being a Nobel laureate.

clue.text: An airbase unusually sited around a large body of water

indicators.note: sited around means the jumbled letters are placed about the single letter that follows
unusually says the letters of an airbase are set out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A military airfield has been oddly built beside a great sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' jumbles AN AIRBASE and 'sited around' puts that jumble round the second A of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This arm of the Indian Ocean, between India and the Arabian peninsula, is a large sea.

clue.text: Organised party machine, originally haphazard

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, past tense ran
a do is a party

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of machine

explanation.surface: A political party's machine was run haphazardly from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random happens by chance, without plan, so it is haphazard.

clue.text: Bonnet and boot

definitions.meaning: a round flat Scottish cap of this name
a laced ankle boot of this name

explanation.definitionFit: Both the Scottish cap and the laced boot take their name from the royal castle in Aberdeenshire.

clue.text: Coming up to Christmas my days are numbered

definitions.text: Coming up to Christmas my days are numbered

parts.words: Coming up to Christmas my days are numbered
parts.note: read as someone's despair before the holiday, it actually describes a card with numbered doors counting the days in December

explanation.definitionFit: A December calendar has numbered windows, one opened each day before Christmas.

clue.text: Sudden increase in power, in second, on drive

parts.note: an urge is a drive or impulse

explanation.surface: An engine gets a burst of power when driven in second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The page breaks 'second' as sec-ond across a line, misread as set-end.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rush, here a spike in electrical power.

clue.text: Smith supporter losing capital?

indicators.note: losing capital says the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a partisan is a committed supporter

explanation.surface: A political supporter of Smith has lost the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smith' looks like a person's name but is the craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith is a metalworker, a skilled craftsman of the manual trades.

clue.text: Court danger and faint, tucking into chilled fish?

indicators.note: tucking into says the word for faint is placed inside the chilled fish

parts.note: a fish kept cold is a skate on ice
thin can mean faint, as in a thin voice

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with danger and then faints while eating cold fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but it signals a container; 'chilled fish' is a fish lying on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk a precarious position is an idiom for courting danger.

clue.text: Paints king wearing a foul weather item

parts.note: oils are paints used by artists
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to be in a coat is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: An artist paints a king who is dressed for bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat of oiled cloth is worn by sailors and fishermen in storms.

clue.text: Young creature always allowed outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for allowed goes round the word for always

parts.note: let means allowed
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A young animal is always permitted to roam outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year is called by this name, a specific baby animal term.

clue.text: Show dogs and horses

parts.note: to point to something is to show it
pointers are gundogs that stand pointing at game

explanation.surface: An event features both show dogs and horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show dogs' looks like a single phrase about dog shows, but 'Show' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses raced in steeplechases across country between landmarks are known by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Roar, to upset speaker

indicators.note: upset says the letters of roar and to are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A loud bellow is used to unsettle someone making a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delivers formal public speeches is a speaker by profession or habit.

clue.text: Lover, capricious soldier

parts.note: fancy can mean whimsical or capricious
a man is an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A fickle soldier is someone's sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: This old British term means a woman's lover, often an illicit one.

clue.text: Time wind swirls — end of December?

definitions.text: Time wind swirls — end of December?

indicators.note: swirls says the letters of time wind are whirled around
end of points to the final letter of December

explanation.surface: Wintry gusts swirl about late in December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirls' jumbles TIMEWIND and the clue as a whole describes the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The solstice in late December marks the deep of winter, a time of year.

clue.text: Where Richmond is unspoilt, I assume initially

parts.note: virgin means untouched or unspoilt

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of assume

explanation.surface: Someone presumes Richmond is a pristine place.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmond is the capital of the US state, not the London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is the state capital of this American state.

clue.text: A racket, uproar bouncing around in slaughterhouse

parts.note: a bat is a racket in table tennis

indicators.note: bouncing around says the word for uproar turns back on itself

parts.note: a riot is an uproar

explanation.surface: A noisy din echoes inside an abattoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncing around' reverses the uproar word; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where animals are killed for meat is a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Regular high fliers in first class, boasted after run

indicators.note: after says the boasted word comes behind the run

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as a letter I
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Frequent flyers sit in first class and brag after a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is read as AI; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane's crew fly regularly at altitude, so they are routine high fliers.

clue.text: Leader's left for Uruguay's capital in a plane

indicators.note: for says one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: a guider is one who leads or guides

indicators.note: capital here means the first letter of Uruguay

explanation.surface: A leader departs to the capital of Uruguay on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader's left' reads as someone departing; actually L replaces the U of GUIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft that flies on air currents is a kind of plane.

clue.text: Book put to one side

definitions.meaning: to book is to make a booking

explanation.definitionFit: Booking a table and setting something aside are both senses of keeping it for later.

clue.text: Bandage half of head following hit

indicators.note: following says the half-word comes after the hit

parts.note: a swat is a hit

indicators.note: half of means the first two letters of head

explanation.surface: A bandage goes round half a head after a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in strips of cloth, as with a bandage.

clue.text: Interesting row developed about a period of buoyancy

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the next word
developed says the letters of interesting row are worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fascinating argument breaks out over a time of economic boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' jumbles INTERESTINGROW and 'about' wraps those letters round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s were a decade of economic boom and lively optimism, a buoyant period.

clue.text: Collect a million as head of security

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of security

explanation.surface: Someone collects a million to serve as chief of security.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather up or accumulate, as in collecting a fortune.

clue.text: Make new alliances with Capone in power

indicators.note: in says the gangster's name is placed inside the word for power

parts.note: reign means rule or power
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster seizes power and forges new partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: To form fresh groupings or partnerships is to realign, a political sense.

clue.text: Tower Hill by rail, mostly

indicators.note: mostly says the word for rail loses its last letter

parts.note: railway track is the rail
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Directions to a London landmark, Tower Hill, by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like the London place; it is one who tows. 'mostly' drops the K of TRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm vehicle that pulls ploughs is something that tows, hence a tower.

clue.text: Refuse to throw away rag

parts.note: to waste something is to throw it away
a rag is a low-quality newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: Someone declines to discard a scrap of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded paper is a kind of rubbish, which is what refuse means as a noun.

clue.text: Release without charge

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to let go is to liberate, and something at no cost is gratis.
